chunks: And Ismaʿīl ibn Abī Ziyād narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.

That Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام asking him about a mentally ill man who killed another man intentionally. So he عليه السلام assigned the blood money to his people and treated his accidental and intentional acts as the same.

key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: blood money; prescribed financial compensation for unlawful killing
key_terms.خَطَأَهُ وَ عَمْدَهُ سَوَاءً: his accidental and intentional acts are treated equally in this ruling
key_terms.رَجُلٍ مَجْنُونٍ: a mentally ill or legally unsound man
key_terms.عَلَى قَوْمِهِ: upon his people; i.e. liability borne by his group

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a mentally ill person intentionally kills someone in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام concerning a mentally ill man who killed another person. The ruling places the diyyah upon his people and treats his intentional and accidental killing alike, indicating a distinct legal status for the acts of one who is majnūn.
